messages:
Rina B.: hi all, newbie onboarding question — I brought up the repo with docker compose and Postgres seems to re-run initialization every restart (extensions like postgis vanish, DB recreated). I'm mounting ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data because I wanted to inspect files. macbook M1, Docker Desktop. Anyone seen this exact re-init+missing-extensions behavior?

Theo Park: welcome Rina! :wave: yep that sounds like the container thinks the PGDATA dir is empty on container start. Official Postgres image decides to initdb if PG_VERSION is missing. Common causes: wrong PGDATA path, permissions/UID mapping on macOS bind mounts, or your dev seed/init scripts overwriting.

Rina B.: PGDATA is not set in my compose file. I just mount ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data. Files appear on host after first run but after compose down/up the container shows an empty /var/lib/postgresql/data. The host folder sometimes has files and sometimes is empty.

Grace Lin: two things to check quickly: (1) Are there any startup scripts under ./docker-entrypoint-initdb.d that unconditionally copy files into PGDATA? (2) Is your compose using a named volume elsewhere with the same name as the host folder (weird name collisions happen).

Rina B.: I do have a small `seed-extensions.sh` in ./dev-helpers that's bound to /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d in the compose file. It unpacks a tar of extension files into /var/lib/postgresql/data. I thought it would only run on first init.

Jules M.: If it's in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d it should only run when the data dir is empty. But on macOS bind mounts the container can see the host mount as empty due to permission/UID mapping or osxfs semantics, causing the init scripts to run again. Also if your script doesn't guard against non-empty but inaccessible dirs (EACCES) it may copy and clobber.

Theo Park: another subtlety: Postgres official image defaults PGDATA to /var/lib/postgresql/data but some versions use a subdir like /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata for safety. If your script writes to one path and the image checks another for PG_VERSION, they can be out of sync. We prefer to explicitly set PGDATA and use a named volume. Example we use in dev: 

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
      - ./dev-helpers:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
volumes:
  pgdata:
```

Theo Park: that avoids osxfs bind-mount ownership weirdness.

Rina B.: ok so switch to named volume. But I want to keep the extension tar on host for editing. Is mounting dev-helpers safe?

Grace Lin: mount only the scripts/configs: `- ./dev-helpers:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro` is fine. But make sure your init script checks `if [ -z "$(ls -A $PGDATA 2>/dev/null)" ]` before copying, and handle permission errors. Example guard: 

```bash
if [ -z "$(ls -A \"$PGDATA\" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  tar -xzf /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/extensions.tar -C "$PGDATA"
fi
```

Grace Lin: also chown the named volume content to 999:999 once after copying so Postgres can write: `docker run --rm -v project_pgdata:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data`

Jules M.: FYI Docker Desktop recently added gRPC FUSE which changes how bind mounts behave. Toggling that option can make a difference for mac M1. We documented that in our setup docs. If you see intermittent empty folders, try switching gRPC FUSE on/off and use a named volume for PGDATA.

Rina B.: good to know. Any migration tip to move my current host ./pgdata content into a named volume without losing the extension files?

Theo Park: quick migration: create volume and copy contents into it in a helper container: 

```bash
docker volume create rina_pgdata
docker run --rm -v rina_pgdata:/data -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/from alpine sh -c "cp -a /from/* /data/ && chown -R 999:999 /data"
```

Theo Park: then update compose to use the volume and start.

Rina B.: thanks! Last question: sometimes my local app (running outside compose) can't reach the DB when I expose ports. I get socket errors. Is that separate?

Jules M.: related. If app runs on host, publish ports (eg `127.0.0.1:5432:5432`) in compose. If app runs as a service inside compose, use service hostname `db`. And avoid leaving ports open publicly on your laptop.

ops-bot: docs/setup.md updated: "Prefer named volumes for PGDATA on macOS; set PGDATA explicitly; mount init scripts only; guard dev seed scripts; see macOS gRPC FUSE note" (https://git.internal/redwood/docs/setup.md) :white_check_mark:

Rina B.: switching to named volume and adding checks to my init script now. Appreciate the help everyone! :sparkles:
